subject: sr-business-studies
title: Staffing and Directing
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: The main purpose of performance appraisal is to —
questions.answer: B

questions.q: Which of the following is an internal source of recruitment?
questions.answer: B

questions.q: Identify the first step of selection process.
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Basic needs like food, clothing and shelter are known as —
questions.answer: C

questions.q: The ability to persuade and motivate others to work in a desired way is called —
questions.answer: D

questions.q: Incentives directly related to money are called —
questions.answer: C

questions.q: Which is the basic monetary incentive?
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Registration card of the employment exchange has to be renewed after —
questions.answer: C

questions.q: Which is the most common print medium for advertisements of job vacancies?
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Which is the closing paragraph of the covering letter sent with a bio-data?
questions.answer: B

questions.q: Vestibule training is a method of —
questions.answer: A

questions.answer: A

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Name the elements of directing (any two).
questions.answer: Communication, supervision, motivation, leadership.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) ______ is the process of telling people what to do and seeing that they do it in the best possible manner. (b) ______ refers to the process by which a person transmits information to another.
questions.answer: (a) Directing. (b) Communication.

questions.q: Give a specific term: (a) Barriers when sender and receiver interpret words and symbols differently. (b) The mode of communication that may be oral or written.
questions.answer: (a) Semantic barriers. (b) Verbal communication.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) ______ results when receiver and sender do not trust each other. (b) The fear of losing authority over subordinates is called ______ barrier.
questions.answer: (a) Distrust (psychological barrier). (b) Personal.

questions.q: Give a specific term: (a) Privately operated organisations that introduce job seekers to employers. (b) Offices set up by the government to bring together job seekers and providers.
questions.answer: (a) Private placement agencies. (b) Employment exchanges.

questions.q: Name the process of finding and attracting suitable applicants; list two of its sources.
questions.answer: Recruitment; internal sources (transfer, promotion) and external sources (advertisements, employment exchanges).

questions.q: State true or false: (i) Staffing is a one-time process. (ii) Training is job oriented.
questions.answer: (i) False. (ii) True.

questions.q: Match: (a) Job description (b) Job specification with (i) statement of duties and responsibilities (ii) qualifications, skills and abilities required.
Name the need in Maslow's hierarchy: (a) respect and recognition (b) love, affection, friendship.
questions.answer: (a) Esteem (ego) needs. (b) Social needs.

questions.q: Give two examples each of financial and non-financial incentives.
questions.answer: Financial: bonus and commission; non-financial: status and recognition.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: A company hires through references of existing employees. Identify the source of recruitment and mention its benefit.
questions.answer: Referrals; the people recommended are known to the company, so the recruitment is reliable, quick and cheap.

questions.q: Name any one internal source of recruitment and give its limitation.
questions.answer: Promotion; limitation: the organisation does not get fresh blood or new ideas.

questions.q: Explain why a selection test is conducted by organisations during the selection process.
questions.answer: To measure the skills, abilities and aptitude of candidates against the job requirements and to eliminate the unsuitable.

questions.q: What is meant by 'Staffing'? / What is meant by 'Training'?
questions.answer: Staffing is employing and developing human resources for managerial and non-managerial jobs; training is increasing the knowledge and skills of an employee for a particular job.

questions.q: (a) Name the process of assignment of job to the selected candidate. (b) Name the process of introducing new employees to the organisation.
questions.answer: (a) Placement. (b) Induction.

questions.q: Distinguish between job description and job specification.
questions.answer: Job description states duties and responsibilities; job specification states the qualifications and skills required.

questions.q: Who is a leader? List two qualities of a good leader.
questions.answer: A person who influences others to follow his instructions; honesty, initiative and communication skill.

questions.q: What is meant by manpower planning?
questions.answer: Estimating the quantity and quality of manpower required by the organisation to get the right number of qualified people at the right time.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: State any three points of importance of the 'staffing' function of management.
questions.answer: It gets the right people for the right job at the right time, improves productivity and gives job satisfaction and harmony.

questions.q: State two advantages and one drawback of internal sources of recruitment.
questions.answer: Advantages: managers know the abilities of their people and employees are happy with recognition of their performance; drawback: no fresh blood.

questions.q: State any three benefits of 'leadership'.
questions.answer: It influences behaviour towards organisational benefit, builds confidence and reduces wastage and builds morale and higher productivity.

questions.q: State any three points of importance of directing function of management.
questions.answer: It guides subordinates, motivates them and maintains discipline and integrates individual with organisational goals.

questions.q: Amit has to recruit 15 salesmen from outside the organisation. Explain any three sources he may use.
questions.answer: Media advertisements, employment exchanges and campus interviews (also referrals, placement agencies).

questions.q: Explain the first two steps of the selection process.
questions.answer: Screening of applications to check eligibility; selection tests to measure skills and abilities.

questions.q: Explain the difference between recruitment and selection (three points).
questions.answer: Recruitment attracts candidates and is positive and simple; selection rejects the unsuitable and is negative and complicated.

questions.q: Explain any three benefits of training to the organisation.
questions.answer: Less wastage, better performance and reduced turnover, absenteeism and accidents.

questions.q: Explain the functions of a supervisor (three).
questions.answer: Clarifies orders, guides and coordinates work and acts as a link between management and workers.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the various types of financial incentives.
questions.answer: Pay and allowances (salary), bonus (cash or trips), commission on sales, retirement benefits (provident fund, pension, gratuity) and perquisites (rent-free accommodation, car allowance).

questions.q: Explain the hierarchy of needs as given by Maslow.
questions.answer: Physiological needs (food, shelter), safety and security, social needs (love and friendship), esteem needs (respect and recognition) and self-actualisation; the next need arises once the lower one is satisfied.

questions.q: Explain the first five steps involved in the process of selection.
questions.answer: Screening of applications, holding selection tests, conducting the interview, checking references and medical examination.

questions.q: List any five specialised activities of a Human Resource Manager.
questions.answer: Manpower planning, recruitment, selection, training and development, performance appraisal, compensation and promotion and transfer (any five).

questions.q: Describe the essential elements of directing.
questions.answer: Communication, supervision, motivation and leadership, each explained with its role.

questions.q: What is meant by training? Explain the different methods of training.
questions.answer: Training increases knowledge and skill for a job; on-the-job methods (coaching, job rotation, understudy) and off-the-job methods (lectures, case discussions, vestibule training).

questions.q: Explain the barriers to effective communication and how to overcome them.
questions.answer: Semantic, psychological, organisational and personal barriers; overcome by consulting others, adjusting to the receiver, clarity, listening and feedback.
